details: U.S. consumer prices rose 0.4% in October, surpassing economists' forecasts and intensifying concerns about further Federal Reserve interest rate hikes. This hotter-than-expected inflation data, coupled with decreased investor appetite and significant Bitcoin ETF outflows, led Bitcoin to fall over 4% on Friday to $68,500, marking its lowest point since mid-August and erasing recent gains. The broader cryptocurrency market also experienced declines as investors sought refuge in yield-bearing assets.
title: US Inflation Reignites Fed Hike Fears, Bitcoin Plunges Below $70K

details: Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh is set to lead a forum on November 16 to explore the impact of artificial intelligence on inflation, productivity, and employment. Some Fed officials have expressed concerns that extensive AI infrastructure spending could sustain elevated inflation, potentially compelling the Federal Reserve to maintain or even further increase interest rates. Such a scenario would make borrowing more costly and could divert capital from speculative assets like cryptocurrencies towards more secure, interest-bearing investments.
title: AI Spending May Keep Inflation High, Pressuring Crypto Markets
